insights.headline: Gold set for weekly loss as December Fed hike odds hit 90%; SEBI curbs, firm rupee shape Diwali-week buying
insights.summary: Spot gold held near $4,165 on Friday but was on track for a ~0.7% weekly loss after hot US inflation pushed the priced-in December Fed hike chance to about 90%; Warsh gave no October signal while Hammack warned of more aggressive hikes. SEBI steered mutual funds to halt fresh gold FoF investments from 16 October, though direct ETF buying stays open. In Delhi, gold held at Rs 1,49,900 per 10g and silver at Rs 2.15 lakh per kg as the rupee's sixth straight gain to 94.92 capped the rebound, while the pullback swung India to a gold premium for the first time in over three months.
points: Spot gold near $4,165 on Friday, on track for a ~0.7% weekly loss; December Fed hike odds at ~90% after hot CPI and PPI.
SEBI-directed halt on fresh gold FoF investments from 16 October; direct gold ETF buying on exchanges stays open.
India swung to a gold premium for the first time in over three months as lower prices lifted festive jewellery demand.
Rupee's sixth straight daily gain to 94.92 capped the domestic rebound in rupee terms.
Silver slid to $57.05, with platinum and palladium also set for weekly losses.

trending.title: December Fed hike bets jump to ~90% as gold heads for weekly loss
trending.summary: Hot US CPI and PPI pushed the priced-in December hike to ~90%; Warsh stayed silent on October while Hammack warned of more aggressive hikes, leaving bullion rangebound.

trending.title: SEBI curbs gold fund-of-funds ahead of Diwali
trending.summary: About 17 fund houses paused fresh FoF subscriptions on SEBI's direction to curb gold-import and rupee pressure; existing SIPs continue and direct ETF buying stays open.

trending.title: Silver lags gold as industrial headwinds bite
trending.summary: Silver broke below $60 to about $55.77 while gold held its range, as weaker industrial demand and substitution pressure weighed on the white metal.

trending.title: Rupee firmness caps the domestic rebound
trending.summary: The rupee's sixth straight gain, to 94.92, and its best week in seven months limited how much of the global bounce reached Indian buyers.

trending.title: Festive demand returns as prices ease
trending.summary: Domestic gold swung to a premium on jewellery buying, and festive-season analyses compared this Dussehra-to-Dussehra run across gold, silver and platinum.

items.title: Gold FoFs halt fresh investments before Diwali: What investors can do
items.summary: About 17 fund houses including Mirae Asset, DSP and Tata have paused fresh lump-sum investments, switch-ins and new SIP/STP registrations into gold ETF funds-of-funds from 15-16 October on SEBI's direction, while existing SIPs, redemptions and direct ETF buying continue. September gold ETF inflows were Rs 4,451 crore.

items.title: Gold set for a weekly drop as traders assess Fed signals
items.summary: Spot gold held near $4,165 on Friday but was set for a ~0.7% weekly loss, with the priced-in December Fed hike chance at about 90% after hot US inflation. Fed Chair Warsh gave no October hint while Cleveland's Hammack warned of more aggressive hikes. Silver fell 0.7% to $57.05; in India, gold traded at a premium for the first time in over three months as the pullback revived jewellery buying.

items.title: India gold swings to premium as lower prices lift jewellery demand
items.summary: Dealers quoted premiums of up to $7 an ounce over official domestic prices this week — India's first premium in over three months — against discounts of up to $6 last week, as lower prices revived jewellery buying. Domestic gold sat near ₹148,200 per 10 grams Friday after a two-week low of ₹145,627. September imports collapsed to $1.8 billion from $9.6 billion a year earlier.

items.title: Why silver is falling faster than gold: What it means for the next surge
items.summary: CPM Group's Jeffrey Christian notes gold consolidating in a $4,050-$4,200 range while silver has broken below $60 to trade near $55.77, arguing silver's larger industrial-demand share and substitution pressure at high prices explain its steeper fall. He flags the risk of a sharper selloff being followed by strong investment demand and a decisive break above $4,200 for gold.

items.title: Gold, silver prices stay steady amid strengthening rupee
items.summary: Delhi gold held at Rs 1,49,900 per 10g and silver at Rs 2.15 lakh per kg as the rupee's sixth straight session of gains (to 94.92 against the dollar) capped a fragile rebound; spot gold was about $4,183 and silver near $57.80. Locally, gold is down Rs 4,500 (3%) and silver Rs 13,500 (6%) on the week.

items.title: Bolivia ends central bank gold purchases, eases export controls
items.summary: Bolivia has scrapped its three-year central-bank gold purchase programme and eased export rules: private exporters can now ship gold without central-bank certification provided at least 80% of prior export value sits in domestic banks. The decree, signed by President Rodrigo Paz's cabinet, aims to lift foreign-currency inflows and dollar availability.

items.title: Fed's Warsh gives no hint on October policy decision
items.summary: At the IMF-World Bank annual meetings in Bangkok, Fed Chair Kevin Warsh said he does not 'prejudge' meetings and gave no preview of the October 27-28 rate decision, after September's quarter-point hike to 3.75-4% -- the first increase in three years. With September CPI running hot at 3.7% year-on-year, markets remain on edge over the timing of the next hike, a key swing factor for gold.

items.title: Rupee posts best week in seven months, fundamentals key for lasting turnaround
items.summary: The rupee gained 2% this week -- its biggest weekly rise in seven months -- closing at 94.96 per dollar, helped by RBI measures including redirecting oil dollar demand and capping undocumented dollar purchases at $5 million. HSBC expects the pair capped in the near term but still sees 96 by year-end, and India's September merchandise trade deficit widened to $30.21 billion.

items.title: India's forex reserves fall $8.58 billion to $726.03 billion: RBI
items.summary: India's forex reserves fell $8.58 billion to $726.03 billion in the week ended October 9, RBI data showed, extending the decline from the September 4 peak of $785.7 billion to nearly $60 billion over six weeks as the central bank sells dollars to defend the rupee. Gold reserves fell $1.32 billion in value to $105.09 billion on price revisions.

items.title: Gold vs silver vs platinum: Which metal saw biggest rally since last Dussehra? Experts explain outlook
items.summary: Silver is the standout since last Dussehra, up about 47% in rupee terms versus gold's ~26% and platinum's ~10.5%; the rupee's slide and the May duty rise to 15% lifted domestic returns. Silver swung wildly, up 155% by January and now 53% off its peak, so buyers near the top stay at a loss. Mint cites experts who see gold backed by central-bank buying, silver with higher upside but more volatility.

items.title: Titan, Senco Gold, Kalyan Jewellers, PC Jeweller: What makes this festive season different?
items.summary: Listed jewellers posted healthy Q2 FY27 growth — Titan jewellery +21% YoY, Kalyan India revenue +27%, Senco +31%, PC Jeweller consolidated +28% — though demand cooled late in the quarter as the festive calendar shifted into Q3. Jewellers remain upbeat on Diwali, Dhanteras and weddings, even as PM Modi's May 2026 appeal to defer gold buying and volatile prices keep volumes the key watch.
